title: Test what users see, not how it's built

slides.say: Here's the idea behind React Testing Library: the more your tests look like real use, the more you can trust them.
Don't reach into state or private functions. Click the button like a user would, then check the text on the screen.

slides.text: Rename a variable or swap useState for useReducer: a good test still passes.
slides.say: The payoff: refactor the inside, rename variables, swap use state for use reducer, and your tests still pass, because the user sees the same thing.

slides.text: Work with DOM nodes, not component instances. If a test breaks, it should be because users would notice.
slides.say: So work with what's on the page, not component internals. When a test fails, it should be for a reason a user would notice.
